chunks: He was sent at a time of hiatus among the Prophets, and a long slumber among the nations,
and a concentration of trials, and a spread of affairs, and a blazing of wars,
and the world was devoid of light, full of deceit,
at a time when its leaves had turned yellow, hope had faded from its fruit, and its water had gone underground,
the signs of guidance had faded, and the signs of destruction had appeared,
so it was stern to its people, frowning in the face of its seeker,
its fruit was trial, its food was carcasses, its banner was fear, and its covering was the sword.

key_terms.فَتْرَة: Hiatus or intermission in prophetic mission

ai.seo_question: What was the state of the world and society when the Prophet Muhammad was sent?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha characterizes the era of Fatr al-Rusul (the hiatus between prophets) as a time of deep spiritual and political decay, where divine guidance had faded and worldly allure masked inner corruption. It highlights the necessity of the Prophet's mission to restore order amidst widespread fitna and war, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of the Prophet as the remedy for a world in its 'dying' phase. The vivid metaphors of a withering tree and darkened light underscore the urgency of divine intervention to reverse the trend of moral decline.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Allāh sent the Prophet when the mission of other Prophets had stopped and the peoples were in slumber for a long time.
Evils were raising heads, all matters were under disruption and in flames of wars,
while the world was devoid of brightness, and full of open deceitfulness.
Its leaves had turned yellow and there was absence of hope about its fruits. While water had gone under-ground.
The minarets of guidance had disappeared and signs of destruction had appeared.
It was stern to its people and frowned in the face of its seeker.
Its fruit was vice and its food was carcass. Its inner dress was fear and outer cover was sword.
